q: Given only a natural-language specification and an empty workspace, an agent must implement a complete, installable project
r: Include: new benchmark where coding agents build whole repositories from natural-language specifications (project level, evaluation method contribution).

q: three production coding agents, four language ecosystems, and 1,000 verified project instances
r: Include: new evaluation framework and metrics for coding agents generating whole projects from prompts, compared across three agents and four ecosystems.
Include: new benchmark and judge for coding agents on repository-level tasks, with 3 runs per configuration and a human study; the contribution is the evaluation method.

q: TESTJACK, an automated framework that audits the successes reported by coding benchmarks
r: EC6: audits patch correctness on issue-repair style benchmarks by generating tests; issue repair and test generation are always excluded.

q: PolyCodeEval, a unified multilingual and multi-granularity benchmark for code generation
r: Include: new benchmark with complete-repository generation level, evaluating LLMs and coding agents under a unified protocol including cost.

q: SWE-DUEL, a self-scaling arena that evaluates coding agents with each other
r: Include: new evaluation method in which agents implement features on real repositories and review each other; the contribution is the evaluation design.
Include: new benchmark for coding agents extending web applications from successive feature requests (feature level).

q: intervention efficacy measures an intervention, such as adding a tool, through paired runs on speedup, success rate and cost
r: Include: main contribution is an evaluation method (paired runs, repetitions, cost metrics, controlled comparison of agents, harnesses and skills), so the domain limit does not exclude it.

q: We propose Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering directly
r: Include: new benchmark where models build a complete harness (an application) from a development document, scored by hidden test cases.

q: Graph Credit, a deterministic, test-grounded metric
r: Include: new multi-PR repository-level task construction and a new metric (Graph Credit) for evaluating code agents; contribution is evaluation method, not single-issue repair.
